name: FEDE Predictive-Causality Framework
description: The FEDE Predictive-Causality Framework is a reproducible software and benchmark package accompanying the study “Beyond RMSE and Granger Gain: Multi-Horizon Forecast-Error Entropy for Nonlinear Predictive Coupling.” The framework quantifies model-relative directed predictive contribution by comparing matched target-only and target-plus-auxiliary forecasts and analyzing the multi-horizon entropy structure of signed forecast errors. The release is designed to reproduce the controlled linear and hidden-nonlinear benchmarks reported in the article and to provide a researcher-facing workflow for applying FEDE to paired time series. The benchmark suite covers calibration to known coupling, weak-coupling detection under process noise, hidden nonlinear extraction, intermittent coupling, direction/source specificity, functional-form robustness, comparisons with out-of-sample Granger-style scores and convergent cross mapping, and robustness to analysis scales. The final package will include Python source code, configuration files, benchmark scripts, reference result tables, figure builders, example data, and an automated analysis/report workflow. Predictive causality is used in the Granger operational sense and does not by itself imply structural or interventional causality.
